mainTopic: Defining the משנה's terms for sewing, bed cords and millstone work on חול המועד, and whether one may cut grooves in millstones on the מועד.
overview: The גמרא explains three rulings from the משנה about work on חול המועד. First it defines a הדיוט, who may sew normally, and מכליב, the changed stitching a professional is allowed to do. Next it asks what מסרגין and ממתחין mean for bed cords. רב דימי's report of the dispute runs into two challenges, one from a ברייתא of רב תחליפא בר שאול and one from a משנה in כלים. So the גמרא brings רבין's version instead: everyone agrees מסרגין means both directions, and the only dispute is about ממתחין. Then a new משנה allows setting up an oven, a stove and a mill. רבי יהודה limits מכבשין on millstones. רב יהודה and רב יחיאל define מכבשין in two different ways, and both definitions survive a challenge from a ברייתא. Finally, רב הונא harshly condemns cutting grooves on חול המועד, following the 'יש אומרים'. רב חמא permits it, and his teaching from רבי מאיר about trimming a riding animal's hooves continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who counts as a layman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a הדיוט may sew normally and asks how we define a הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a layman may sew in his usual way. The גמרא asks: what kind of person counts as a layman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks for a definition. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On חול המועד, sewing is allowed only if it is not skilled, professional work. So the גמרא needs a clear line between a הדיוט, who may sew normally, and an אומן, who may not.

keyTerms.meaning: A layman; someone who is not a skilled professional
What is the case? How do we define it?

phrases.english: A layman may sew in his usual manner.
What are the circumstances of a layman?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A working definition of who counts as a הדיוט for the sewing leniency.

steps.title: Can't pull a full needle at once
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי says a הדיוט is someone who cannot pull a needle full of stitches through the cloth in one motion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: anyone who cannot pull a full needle of stitches through the cloth in one go is a layman.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer to the question: the test for a הדיוט is skill with the needle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A skilled tailor can load several stitches onto the needle and pull them all through at once. Someone who can't do this sews slowly, one stitch at a time, so his sewing doesn't count as professional work.

keyTerms.meaning: A full needle, meaning a needle loaded with several stitches

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
Anyone who is not able
to pull a full needle through at one time.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הדיוט is one who cannot pull a full needle of stitches through at once.

steps.title: Can't sew a straight hem
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא gives a different test: a הדיוט is someone who cannot sew a straight seam on the hem of his shirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: anyone who cannot sew a straight seam on the hem of his shirt is a layman.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different way to define a הדיוט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This test looks at the quality of the result, a straight and even hem, instead of speed with the needle. If a person can't even sew a neat hem on his own shirt, he is clearly not a skilled tailor.

keyTerms.meaning: The hem (folded edge) of his shirt

steps.whatToRemember: There are two tests for a הדיוט: he can't pull a full needle through at once (דבי רבי ינאי), or he can't sew a straight hem (רבי יוסי בר חנינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
Anyone who is not able to line up straight
a seam on the hem of his shirt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different definition alongside the school of רבי ינאי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הדיוט is one who cannot sew a straight seam on his shirt's hem.

steps.title: What is מכליב stitching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a professional may only do מכליב stitching, and asks what מכליב means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a craftsman may only do מכליב stitching. The גמרא asks: what does מכליב mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line in the משנה, about the professional tailor, and asks what an unclear word means. Two answers follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A professional's normal sewing is real skilled work, so he can't sew normally on חול המועד. The משנה allows him only a changed, weaker kind of stitching, and the גמרא wants to know exactly what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: Sews loose or irregular stitches (the meaning is discussed here)
What is? What does it mean?

phrases.english: And the craftsman may do makhliv stitching.
What is makhliv?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of מכליב, the limited stitching allowed to a professional.

steps.title: Skipping stitches
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains מכליב as מפסיע, sewing with gaps by skipping stitches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: מכליב means he skips, leaving spaces between stitches.
steps.whatsHappening: The first explanation of מכליב: the professional leaves gaps instead of sewing a full, tight seam.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because stitches are skipped, the result is clearly not his normal professional work. That change is what makes it allowed on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes big steps, meaning he skips and leaves gaps between stitches

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: He skips.
phrases.notes: Literally 'he takes steps', so the stitches are spaced apart with gaps.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מכליב means sewing with skipped stitches (gaps).

steps.title: Dog's-teeth stitches
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל explains מכליב as stitches shaped like a dog's teeth, uneven and not in a straight line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said: מכליב means stitches like the teeth of a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation of מכליב: the stitches are crooked and uneven, like a dog's teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the change is in the shape of the stitches rather than gaps between them. The word מכליב even sounds like כלב (dog), which fits this explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Teeth of a dog; crooked, uneven stitches

steps.whatToRemember: A professional on חול המועד may only sew in a changed way: either with skipped stitches (רבי יוחנן) or with uneven dog's-teeth stitches (רבה בר שמואל).

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אֲמַר: שִׁינֵּי כַלְבְּתָא.
phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel said: The teeth of a dog.
phrases.notes: He means the stitches go up and down unevenly, the way a dog's teeth do.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אֲמַר: שִׁינֵּי כַלְבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different meaning of מכליב than רבי יוחנן's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מכליב means crooked, uneven stitches like a dog's teeth.

steps.title: What are interweaving and tightening?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one may do מסרגין on beds and asks what מסרגין and ממתחין mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may interweave the cords of beds. The גמרא asks: what does 'interweave' mean, and what does 'tighten' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's ruling about bed cords and asks for the meaning of two words. This sets up רב דימי's report in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר allows מסרגין, while רבי יוסי allows only ממתחין. To understand their argument, we need to know what each kind of work actually involves.

keyTerms.meaning: Interweaving (stringing) the cords of a bed
Beds; here, the cord webbing of a bed frame

phrases.english: One may interweave the cords of beds.
What is 'interweaving' and what is 'tightening'?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meanings of מסרגין and ממתחין from the משנה's dispute.

steps.title: First view: lengthwise and widthwise
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי אסי disagree. One says מסרגין is stringing cords both lengthwise and widthwise, while ממתחין is lengthwise only.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי חייא בר אבא and רבי אסי disagree about this, and both report in the name of חזקיה and רבי יוחנן. One said: interweaving is lengthwise and widthwise, and tightening is lengthwise without widthwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a report from ארץ ישראל of two opposite explanations. This step gives the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, מסרגין (רבי מאיר) is a full web of cords in both directions. ממתחין (רבי יוסי) is only the lengthwise cords, which is less work. So רבי יוסי is stricter and allows only half the job.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Lengthwise and widthwise (like warp and weft in weaving)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא וְרַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Asi disagree about it,
and both of them in the name of Ḥizkiyya and Rabbi Yoḥanan.
One said: Interweaving is lengthwise and widthwise,
and tightening is lengthwise without widthwise.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מסרגין is cords in both directions; ממתחין is lengthwise cords only.

steps.title: Second view: tightening loose cords
steps.stepSummary: The other view says מסרגין is lengthwise only, and ממתחין means only tightening a cord that became loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: interweaving is lengthwise without widthwise, and tightening means that if a cord was loose, he tightens it.
steps.whatsHappening: The second explanation shifts both words one level down. What the first view called ממתחין is now called מסרגין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, even רבי מאיר allows only lengthwise cords. רבי יוסי allows no new stringing at all, only tightening a cord that is already there and has gone slack.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the shift: 'lengthwise without widthwise' means ממתחין in the first view but מסרגין in the second view. Keep track of which view you are reading.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: מְסָרְגִין — שְׁתִי בְּלֹא עֵרֶב,
phrases.english: And one said: Interweaving is lengthwise without widthwise,
and tightening is that if it was loose, he tightens it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר: מְסָרְגִין — שְׁתִי בְּלֹא עֵרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing explanation in the same dispute reported by רב דימי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מסרגין is lengthwise only; ממתחין is just tightening an existing loose cord.

steps.title: Challenge: no braiding new cords
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions these explanations using a ברייתא of רב תחליפא בר שאול: everyone agrees one may not braid cords from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב תחליפא בר שאול taught: and they agree that one may not braid cords from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with a ברייתא. It says both sides of the משנה agree on one limit: no braiding new cords.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree that new cords may not be made, then each explanation of their argument has to leave room for that shared limit. The גמרא is about to check which explanation fits.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (both sides of the dispute)
From the start; here, making new cords

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי? וְהָא תָּנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר שָׁאוּל:
phrases.english: Is that so? But Rav Taḥlifa bar Shaul taught:
And they agree that one may not braid cords from the start.
phrases.notes: 'They' means both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא תָּנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר שָׁאוּל
steps.kashyaTarget: The second explanation in רב דימי's report (מסרגין is lengthwise only; ממתחין is tightening a loose cord), which אִינִי pushes back on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says both sides agree that new cords may not be braided, so any explanation of the dispute must fit this shared limit.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits the first view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא fits well with the first view (מסרגין is both directions, ממתחין is lengthwise only). This sets up a problem for the second view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who said interweaving is lengthwise and widthwise, and tightening is lengthwise without widthwise. That is what רב תחליפא בר שאול teaches: and they agree that one may not braid cords from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the 'בשלמא' pattern, the גמרא first shows which view the ברייתא fits. This prepares the next move, where it will challenge the other view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first view, both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי allow stringing new cords onto the bed in some form. So the ברייתא has to tell us that both still forbid braiding brand-new cords. The 'בשלמא' wording signals that the second view will have trouble, and the גמרא explains that next.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (sets up a contrast with a view that has a problem)
According to the one who said
That is what is taught; this fits the teaching

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who said
interweaving is lengthwise and widthwise,
and tightening is lengthwise without widthwise:

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר שָׁאוּל:
phrases.english: that is what Rav Taḥlifa bar Shaul teaches:
and they agree that one may not braid cords from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops the challenge from the ברייתא by first showing which view it fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second explanation (מסרגין is lengthwise only; ממתחין is tightening loose cords).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא fits the first view naturally. The 'בשלמא' pattern signals that the second view will be challenged next.

steps.title: The second view makes the ברייתא say something obvious
steps.stepSummary: If מסרגין means lengthwise only and ממתחין means tightening a loose cord, then nobody ever allows lengthwise-and-widthwise. In that case, there is no need for the ברייתא to say that everyone forbids making new cords. The גמרא admits this is a real difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says interweaving is lengthwise only and tightening is fixing a loose cord: now that you said even lengthwise-and-widthwise is not allowed, do we need to be told that making cords from scratch is forbidden?! It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the attack it began in the last step. It shows that the second view leaves the ברייתא saying something too obvious to need saying, and it ends with קשיא, meaning 'this remains a problem.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the second view, even the most lenient opinion only allows lengthwise stringing. Lengthwise-and-widthwise is then forbidden by everyone. Making brand-new cords is an even bigger job, so it is obviously forbidden too, and the ברייתא would have no reason to state it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it necessary to say? (it is obvious)
It is a difficulty; the problem stands

steps.confusionAlert: Here קַשְׁיָא means the problem stands with no answer. The גמרא does not try to save this view. After a second challenge in step 13, it drops רב דימי's report and brings רבין's version instead (step 14).

phrases.english: But according to the one who said
interweaving means lengthwise without widthwise,

phrases.aramaic: מְמַתְּחִין — שֶׁאִם הָיָה רָפוּי הָיָה מְמַתְּחוֹ.
phrases.english: and tightening means that if a cord was loose, he would tighten it:
now that you said lengthwise-and-widthwise is not allowed,
is it necessary to say that making cords from scratch is forbidden?!
It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא שְׁתִי וָעֵרֶב אָמְרַתְּ לָא — חֲבָלִים לְכַתְּחִלָּה מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 11 set up, now aimed at the second view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second view (מסרגין = lengthwise only; ממתחין = tightening a loose cord)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this view nobody permits both directions, so the ברייתא's ruling that everyone forbids new cords would be obvious and unnecessary.

steps.title: A משנה shows that סירוג always means both directions
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks whether anyone could really hold that מסרגין is lengthwise only. A משנה quotes רבי מאיר saying a bed becomes a usable vessel once three 'houses' (squares) are woven. Squares need both lengthwise and widthwise cords.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבי חייא בר אבין: Is there really someone who says interweaving is lengthwise without widthwise? But we learned in a משנה that רבי מאיר says: a bed counts once one has interwoven three meshes in it!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge attacks the second view directly. It asks whether that view can even exist, since a משנה uses the word סירוג for weaving squares, and squares need both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יסרג' (from the same root as מסרגין) describes making 'בתים', squares. You cannot make a square with lengthwise cords alone. This proves that the word סירוג itself means both directions, so the second view's definition does not fit how the word is used.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'houses': the squares formed by crossing cords
He interweaves (the same root as מְסָרְגִין)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said
to Rabbi Chiya bar Avin:
Is there anyone who says
that interweaving means lengthwise without widthwise?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Meir says:
A bed counts as a vessel from when one interweaves three meshes in it!
phrases.notes: That משנה is about when a bed can become טמא. 'Meshes' are little squares, and squares need cords going both ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְסָרְגִין — שְׁתִי בְּלֹא עֵרֶב? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger challenge to the second view, this time from a משנה about how the word סירוג is used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of מסרגין as lengthwise only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה uses סירוג for weaving squares, which requires both directions, so מסרגין cannot mean lengthwise only.

steps.title: רבין's version: the dispute is only about ממתחין
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports the dispute differently. Everyone agrees מסרגין means both directions. The two אמוראים disagree only about ממתחין: one says it means lengthwise only, the other says it means tightening a loose cord.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came, he said: About interweaving, everyone agrees it means lengthwise and widthwise. They disagree only about tightening. One master holds tightening means lengthwise without widthwise, and one master holds it means tightening a cord that became loose.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier report ran into problems, the גמרא brings a different report of the same dispute from רבין. This version avoids both difficulties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both opinions agree with the משנה in כלים that סירוג means both directions. The argument moves to the word ממתחין. Either it means simple lengthwise stringing, or it means only tightening a cord that is already there and has gone slack.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל) with a teaching
Everyone agrees; there is no dispute

steps.whatToRemember: In רבין's version, מְסָרְגִין means both directions according to everyone. The only argument is whether מְמַתְּחִין means lengthwise stringing or just tightening a loose cord.

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came, he said:
About interweaving, everyone agrees
that it is lengthwise and widthwise;
rather, where they disagree is about tightening.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר מְמַתְּחִין — שְׁתִי בְּלֹא עֵרֶב,
phrases.english: One master holds tightening means lengthwise without widthwise,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: שֶׁאִם הָיָה רָפוּי מְמַתְּחוֹ.
phrases.english: and one master holds it means that if a cord was loose, he tightens it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב דימי's report, which was challenged in steps 12-13, with a new version of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate transmission of the dispute (a different report of what the אמוראים argued about)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אמוראים disagreed about what מסרגין means, with one view saying lengthwise only.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees מסרגין is both directions; the disagreement is only about the meaning of ממתחין.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought to challenge רבין's version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with three opinions. רבי מאיר allows interweaving and, even more so, tightening. רבי יוסי allows tightening but not interweaving. 'Some say' one may not tighten at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One may interweave a bed, and needless to say one may tighten it; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: one may tighten but not interweave. And some say: one may not tighten at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in order to challenge רבין's version. This step sets up the source; the exact problem is spelled out right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a range: one opinion allows both actions, one allows only tightening, and one allows no tightening at all. The גמרא will test whether this range of opinions fits with how רבין's version defines ממתחין.

keyTerms.meaning: And needless to say (all the more so)
Some say (an unnamed opinion in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One may interweave a bed,
and needless to say one may tighten;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:
One may tighten, but not interweave.
And some say:
One may not tighten at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבין's version from step 14 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's version of the dispute about ממתחין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's three opinions about interweaving and tightening will be tested against רבין's definitions; the specific problem is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: How could the strictest view forbid even tightening a loose cord?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's 'יש אומרים' fits the first explanation of ממתחין, but under the second explanation they would forbid even tightening a loose cord. That seems far too strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says ממתחין means lengthwise cords without widthwise ones. That is why 'יש אומרים' comes to disagree. But for the one who says ממתחין means tightening a loose cord, would 'יש אומרים' forbid even tightening it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the ברייתא from step 15 against both explanations of ממתחין. It finds that the second explanation leads to a very strict result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ממתחין means putting in new lengthwise cords, then 'יש אומרים' only forbids adding new cords and can still allow tightening a loose one. If ממתחין means tightening a loose cord, then 'יש אומרים' forbids even that tiny repair. That seems hard to accept, because a person needs a usable bed.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces the side that works, before the side that has a problem)
'Some say', the third and strictest opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who said
"tightening" means lengthwise without widthwise:
that is why "some say" comes to disagree.
But according to the one who said
that if it was loose, he tightens it,
according to "some say", may he not even tighten it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the three-opinion ברייתא from step 15 to test the second explanation of ממתחין from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that ממתחין means tightening a loose cord.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that view, 'יש אומרים' would ban even tightening a loose cord, which seems unreasonably strict, since a person needs a bed he can sleep in.

steps.title: Yes, because the bed can be filled with clothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the strict result: 'יש אומרים' really does forbid tightening, because the sagging spot can be filled with clothes instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Since it is possible to fill it with clothing, we do not go to the trouble of fixing it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by accepting it. 'יש אומרים' really does forbid even tightening a loose cord.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that the bed is not really unusable. The person can stuff clothing into the sagging spot and sleep there, so there is no need to bother fixing the bed on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: We go to trouble / exert ourselves

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבין's version, everyone agrees מסרגין means both directions. Under the view that ממתחין means tightening a loose cord, 'יש אומרים' forbids even that, because one can fill the sagging bed with clothing.

phrases.english: Yes,
since it is possible to fill it with clothing,
we do not go to the trouble.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 16 by accepting its conclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the conclusion and justifying it (אין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding the tightening of a loose cord would leave the person without a usable bed, so no one could hold this.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is an easy alternative, filling the dip with clothing, so the repair is unnecessary and is forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.title: משנה: setting up an oven, stove and mill on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה permits setting up an oven, a stove and a mill on חול המועד. רבי יהודה says one may not do מכבשין to the millstones for the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may set up an oven, a stove and a mill on חול המועד. רבי יהודה says: one may not chisel the millstones for the first time.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: setting up household appliances on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion permits setting up these three items. רבי יהודה adds a limit: one may not do מכבשין to millstones for the first time. What מכבשין means is left unclear, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Chiseling or working the millstones (its exact meaning is debated next)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may set up an oven, a stove, and a mill on the Festival.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
One may not chisel the millstones for the first time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The bed-cord discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting up an oven, stove and mill is permitted on חול המועד. רבי יהודה forbids מכבשין of millstones for the first time.

steps.title: What does מכבשין mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what work רבי יהודה means by the word מכבשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is מכבשין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the meaning of an unclear word in the משנה. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot know what רבי יהודה forbids until we know what kind of work on the mill מכבשין refers to.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is "chiseling"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact kind of mill work that the word מכבשין refers to.

steps.title: Two explanations: cutting grooves or cutting the eyehole
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says מכבשין means cutting grooves into the millstones. רב יחיאל says it means cutting the eyehole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: cutting grooves into the millstone. רב יחיאל said: the eyehole.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים each give a different definition of מכבשין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה says it means roughening the millstone's surface with grooves so it grinds properly. רב יחיאל says it means cutting the hole in the upper stone where the grain goes in. Either way, this is the work רבי יהודה forbids doing for the first time on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Pecking or cutting grooves into the millstone
The 'eyehole', the opening in the upper millstone

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב יהודה the אמורא here with רבי יהודה the תנא in the משנה. רב יהודה is explaining רבי יהודה's word.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said:
Cutting grooves into the millstone.
רב יחיאל said:
The eyehole.
phrases.notes: Literally "daughter of the eye". It's the hole in the upper stone where the grain drops in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 with two different definitions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יהודה: cutting grooves into the millstones. רב יחיאל: cutting the eyehole in the upper millstone.

steps.title: A ברייתא about ovens, stoves and millstones on the מועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר allows setting up an oven and stove without finishing; the חכמים allow finishing; רבי יהודה in רבי אליעזר's name allows setting up a new mill and doing מכבשין to an old one; 'יש אומרים' forbid מכבשין entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: One may set up an oven and a stove on the מועד, as long as he does not finish the work; these are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: he may even finish. רבי יהודה says in his name: one may set up a new millstone and do מכבשין to an old one. And some say: one may not do מכבשין at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a ברייתא to set up a challenge. The real question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that רבי יהודה allows מכבשין on an OLD millstone. The גמרא will now check whether both explanations of מכבשין from step 20 make sense for an old stone.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as he does not finish
The new one / the old one (millstone)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One may set up an oven and a stove on the Festival,
provided that he does not complete their work,
the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
But the Sages say: he may even complete it.
Rabbi Yehuda says in his name:
One may set up the new one,
phrases.notes: "The new one" is a new millstone.

phrases.english: and one may do mechabshin to the old one.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מְכַבְּשִׁין כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: And some say: one may not do mechabshin at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the two explanations of מכבשין given in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מכבשין is allowed on an old millstone according to רבי יהודה quoting רבי אליעזר; 'יש אומרים' forbid it entirely.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יחיאל's explanation of מכבשין as cutting the eyehole (step 20).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets רבי יהודה do מכבשין on an OLD millstone. Both definitions from step 20 must make sense for an old stone. The next step spells out the problem.

steps.title: Why would an old millstone need an eyehole?
steps.stepSummary: Cutting grooves fits an old millstone, but an old millstone already has an eyehole, so רב יחיאל's explanation seems not to fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who said מכבשין means cutting grooves in the millstone: that is something you find with an old stone. But for the one who said it means the eyehole: an old stone, why does it need an eyehole?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יחיאל's explanation, using the ברייתא's word 'old'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old millstones wear smooth, so re-cutting grooves makes sense. But every working millstone already has its eyehole, so cutting one into an OLD stone seems pointless, which suggests רב יחיאל is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for one view, but...)
The eyehole (center hole of the millstone)

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said
mechabshin means cutting grooves in the millstone —
that is how you find it with an old one,
but according to the one who said it means the eyehole,
an old one — why does it need an eyehole?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's word 'old' to attack the second explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יחיאל's explanation that מכבשין means cutting the eyehole.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An old millstone already has an eyehole, so the ברייתא's permission for an old stone makes no sense under this explanation.

steps.title: He wants to widen the hole a little
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about someone who wants to make the existing eyehole a bit wider.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he wants to widen it a little more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יחיאל by showing a case where an old stone does need eyehole work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old stone does have a hole, but sometimes it needs to be made a little bigger. So 'doing מכבשין to an old stone' can mean widening the eyehole, and רב יחיאל's explanation still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּקָא בָּעֵי לְאַרְווֹחֵי טְפֵי פּוּרְתָּא.
phrases.english: For example, where he wants to widen it a little more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב יחיאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא refers to widening an existing hole.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An old millstone has no use for eyehole work, so רב יחיאל's explanation fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Widening the existing eyehole counts, so both explanations fit the ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: Both explanations of מכבשין survive: grooves can be re-cut in an old stone, and an old stone's eyehole can be widened.

steps.title: רב הונא curses a man cutting grooves on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא heard a man cutting grooves in his millstone on חול המועד and harshly said that the man's body should be desecrated, since he desecrates the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא heard a certain man cutting grooves into a millstone on חול המועד. He said: Who is this? May his body be desecrated, for he is desecrating חול המועד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that רב הונא held cutting grooves in a millstone is forbidden on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting grooves is exactly what רב יהודה called מכבשין. רב הונא treated it as a real violation of the מועד, with a measure-for-measure curse: he 'desecrated' the day, so may his body be 'desecrated'.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of the Festival
May his body be desecrated (a curse)

phrases.english: Rav Huna heard a certain man
cutting grooves into a millstone on the intermediate days of the Festival,
He said: Who is this?
May his body be desecrated,
for he desecrates the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining מכבשין to how an אמורא actually ruled on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב הונא, cutting grooves into a millstone on חול המועד is forbidden.

steps.title: רב הונא holds like the 'יש אומרים'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא follows the 'יש אומרים' in the ברייתא, who forbid מכבשין entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the 'some say' opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which opinion in the ברייתא רב הונא was following.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's view allows מכבשין on an old millstone, so רב הונא could not be following him. He must follow the 'יש אומרים', who say מכבשין is not allowed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: "Some say": the strictest opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with "some say."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis of רב הונא's strict reaction in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא rules like the 'יש אומרים': no מכבשין on millstones at all on the מועד.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not the same person as רב יהודה from step 20. רב הונא's anger fits the strict 'יש אומרים', not the more lenient רבי יהודה of the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב חמא: one may cut grooves in millstones on the מועד
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא publicly taught that cutting grooves into millstones is permitted on the מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא taught publicly: One may cut grooves into millstones on the מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב חמא's public teaching, which is the opposite of רב הונא's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא forbade cutting grooves; רב חמא openly permits it. This matches the lenient side of the ברייתא, not the 'יש אומרים'.

keyTerms.meaning: One may cut grooves into millstones

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama taught publicly:
One may cut grooves into millstones on the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a lenient ruling that disagrees with רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting grooves into millstones is permitted on חול המועד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the אמוראים split on this practical question: רב הונא forbids, רב חמא permits.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: one may even trim a riding animal's hooves
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא quotes רבי מאיר that it is permitted on חול המועד to trim the hooves of a horse or donkey that one rides.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי מאיר he said: Even a horse that he rides and a donkey that he rides, it is permitted to trim their hooves on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא adds a further lenient teaching, quoted from רבי מאיר, about caring for riding animals on חול המועד. The sentence continues into the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' signals that this is a notable leniency: trimming the hooves of an animal one rides is allowed on the מועד. The sentence is not finished here and continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Meir he said:
Even a horse that he rides upon
and a donkey that he rides upon —
it is permitted to trim the nails
phrases.notes: For an animal, the "nails" are its hooves.

phrases.english: on the intermediate days of the Festival,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חמא's lenient teaching with a quote from רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trimming the hooves of a riding horse or donkey is permitted on חול המועד.
